title: PRII gate attestation
description: A signed, machine-produced claim about a property no execution can demonstrate: code that must never run, an absence, or a host this process is not running on. Verified exactly like a receipt, so a gate bound to an attestation is still derived rather than asserted. An attestation is not an annotation and carries no free-text status.

attestation_id.description: Stable dotted identifier a GateRule binds to, e.g. static.no_arbitrary_shell.

kind.description: Closed set. Adding a kind should be a deliberate act, not something invented at a call site.

produced_by.description: The test node id or script that produced this claim, so a reader can re-run it.

result.description: 'refuted' makes a bound gate 'failed', never 'not_run' -- we checked and it did not hold, which is a finding rather than an absence.

environment.description: Where the claim was produced. An operator_certification attestation naming a Linux platform is self-evidently not macOS evidence.

details.description: Whatever makes the claim auditable: counts scanned, boundaries exercised, steps completed.
